{{small|(21)}} | details = | date = {{start date|2026|7|19|df=y}} | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Cathal O'Neill]]{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/cathal-oneill-limerick-man-of-the-match-7107664-Jul2026/|title=Cathal O'Neill's brilliant 1-4 earns him All-Ireland final Man of the Match award|first=Niall|last=Kelly|website=www.the42.ie|date=20 July 2026|accessdate=20 July 2026}} | referee = Colm Lyons (Cork) | weather = {{cvt|21|C}}, sunny{{Cite web |date=19 July 2026 |title=Weather in Dublin, 19 July 2026 |url=https://world-weather.info/forecast/ireland/dublin/19-july/ |access-date=20 July 2026 |website=World Weather Info}} | previous = [[2025 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2025]] | next = [[2027 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2027]] }} The '''2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 19 July 2026 between [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]],{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0704/1581739-galway-devour-shell-shocked-cork-to-reach-decider/|title= Galway devour shell-shocked Cork to reach decider|date=4 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=6 July 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0705/1581834-oconnor-goal-sees-limerick-snatch-victory-at-the-death/|title= Aidan O'Connor goal sees Limerick snatch victory at the death|date=5 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=6 July 2026}} the culmination of the [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|139th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Limerick won the match on a scoreline of 1–29 to 1–18, it was their sixth All-Ireland title since 2018.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0719/1584049-limerick-regain-crown-with-emphatic-demolition-of-galway/|title=Limerick regain hurling crown with emphatic demolition of Galway|date=19 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=24 July 2026}}{{cite web|url= https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/all-ireland-final/irresistible-limerick-regain-all-ireland-title-with-stunning-win-over-galway-8809558|title=Irresistible Limerick regain All-Ireland title with stunning win over Galway|date=19 July 2026|work=Limerick Leader|accessdate=24 July 2026}}{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2026/07/19/galway-v-limerick-live-all-ireland-hurling-final-updates-western-forces-clash-at-croke-park/|title=All-Ireland hurling final: Limerick beat Galway by 11 points – as it happened|date=19 July 2026|work=Irish Times|accessdate=24 July 2026}} The match was televised nationally on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park pitch with analysis by [[Joe Canning]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The game was also televised on [[BBC Two]], and streamed on [[iPlayer]] and [[GAA+]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0714/1583304-all-ireland-hurling-final-all-you-need-to-know/|title= All-Ireland hurling final: All you need to know|date=16 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=16 July 2026}} {{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cgl3rww488lo|title= Galway must make 'a good start' against Limerick|date=16 July 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 July 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/mediacentre/2026/live-coverage-gaa-all-ireland-finals|title= Live coverage across the BBC of the GAA All-Ireland Senior Hurling and Football Championship finals|date=16 July 2026|work=BBC|accessdate=16 July 2026}} ==Background== {{Main|Galway–Limerick hurling rivalry}} *{{GG|Limerick|hurling}} were aiming to win their 13th All-Ireland title, and their first since [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2023]]; they had been the dominant team in hurling in recent years, with All-Irelands in 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 and [[National Hurling League]] wins in 2019, 2020, 2023 and 2026.{{Cite web|url=https://www.limerick.ie/council/newsroom/news/limericks-historic-links-with-the-gaa|title=Limerick's historic links with the GAA|date=20 July 2023|website=www.limerick.ie}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0317/1563852-allianz-hurling-league-r7-all-you-need-to-know/|title=Allianz Hurling League R7: All You Need to Know|first=Conor|last=Neville|date=17 March 2026|via=www.rte.ie}} *{{GG|Galway|hurling}} were aiming to win their 6th All-Ireland title and their first since [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2017]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.galwaygaa.ie/history/all-ireland-winning-teams/|title=All Ireland Winning Teams – Galway GAA}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0717/1583905-all-ireland-final-a-crown-jewel-amongst-sporting-riches/|title=All-Ireland SHC final a crown jewel amongst sporting riches|date=18 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=24 July 2026}} *The fourth meeting of Galway and Limerick in the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|final]]. Limerick won in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2018 final]], while Galway were the winners when the two counties met in [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1923]] and [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1980]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0815/985359-from-1973-to-now-limericks-long-wait-for-glory/ |title =From 1973 to now: Limerick's long wait for glory|date=18 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2018}} ==Paths to the final== {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} {| class="wikitable" |+ Galway |- !Round!! border-top:3px solid black" | All-Ireland SHC semi-final || 5 July 2026 || [[File:Colours of Clare.svg|border|20x20px]] {{GG|Clare|hurling}} || [[Croke Park]] (N) || align="center"| Win ||align="center"| 2 || align="center"|1–21 to 1–19 || {{Cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41874398.html|title=Late goal sees Limerick survive intense Clare test to book All-Ireland final return|date=5 July 2026|website=echo live}} |} {{col-end}} ==Pre-match== ===Tickets=== Tickets for the match sold-out and were distributed by the clubs with no public sale and priced at €100 for the stands and €55 for the terrace.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/brainstorm/2025/0707/1518663-gaa-croke-park-all-ireland-final-ticket-allocations-hurling-football/|title=How do you get your hands on All Ireland final tickets?|date=14 July 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=15 July 2025}} ===Officials=== On 8 July, the GAA named [[Cork GAA|Cork]]'s Colm Lyons from [[Nemo Rangers GAA|Nemo Rangers]] as the referee for the final, his second All-Ireland SHC decider, he previously refereed the [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022 final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/colm-lyons-to-referee-all-ireland-shc-final-x9710|title=Colm Lyons to referee All-Ireland SHC Final|date=8 July 2026|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=9 July 2026}} It was his 39th All-Ireland Championship game to referee since his first in 2012. His umpires were Ciarán Hanley, Jim McEvoy, Philip Mackey and Finian Mullane. Line umpires were Wexford’s James Owens and Dublin’s Chris Mooney. James Owens was also the standby referee, and the sideline official was Niall Malone from Clare. David Grogan from Tipperary was the [[Hawk-Eye]] official.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0708/1582428-lyons-appointed-to-referee-all-ireland-hurling-final/|title=Colm Lyons appointed to referee All-Ireland Hurling Championship final|date=8 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=9 July 2026}} ===Jubilee team=== The [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] team that won the [[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2001 All-Ireland SHC final]] was presented to the crowd before the match, on the [[silver jubilee]].{{Cite web|url=https://tipperary.gaa.ie/2001-all-ireland-senior-hurling-champions-jubilee-golf-classic/|title=2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Champions Jubilee Golf Classic|first=Tipp GAA|last=Admin|date=29 May 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.tipperarylive.ie/sport/gaa/watch-tipperary-2001-team-honoured-in-croke-park-ahead-of-all-ireland-final-8810192|title= WATCH: Tipperary 2001 team honoured in Croke Park ahead of All-Ireland final|date=20 July 2026|work=Tipperary Live|accessdate=22 July 2026}} ===Team news=== For Limerick, captain [[Cian Lynch]] was recalled to the starting team in midfield, with Darragh O'Donovan dropping out. [[Mike Casey (hurler)|Mike Casey]] also started at full-back. The Galway team announced was unchanged from the semi-final win against Cork.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0717/1583800-aishc-final-team-news-galway-unchanged-from-semi-final/|title=AISHC final team news: Cian Lynch returns, Galway unchanged from semi-final|date=17 July 2026|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=24 July 2026}} ==Match== ===Details=== {{GAAmatchbox |date={{start date|2026|7|19|df=y}} |time=15:30 {{small|[[Irish Standard Time|IST]] ([[UTC+1]])}} |round=Final |team1=[[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] [[File:Colours of Galway.svg|border|20x20px]] |score1=1–18 {{small|(21)}} |score2= {{small|(32)}} 1–29 |HT=0-8 – 0-13 |report=[https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41882305.html Report] |team2=[[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|border|20x20px]] [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] |goals1=Conor Cooney 1(pen) |points1=Aaron Niland 10 (8fs, 1 '65'), Conor Cooney 2 (1f), Thomas Monaghan 2, Cathal Mannion 1, Darragh Neary 1, Jason Rabbitte 1, Colm Molloy 1 |goals2=Cathal O’Neill 1 |points2=Aidan O’Connor 5 (3fs), Cathal O’Neill 4, Aaron Gillane 4, Peter Casey 4, Diarmaid Byrnes 4 (2fs, 1 '65'), Kyle Hayes 2, Adam English 2, Cian Lynch 2, Barry Nash 1, David Reidy 1 |location=[[Dublin]] |venue=[[Croke Park]] |attendance=82,300 |referee= Colm Lyons ([[Cork GAA|Cork]]) |standby = James Owens ([[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]) |linesman = Chros Mooney ([[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]) |sideline = Niall Malone ([[Clare GAA|Clare]]) |umpires = Ciarán Hanley ([[Brian Dillons GAA|Brian Dillons]]), Jim McEvoy ([[Blarney GAA|Blarney]]), Philip Mackey & Finian Mullane ([[Nemo Rangers GAA|Nemo Rangers]]) |TV=[[RTÉ2]]
